# WaniKani API Manager

A JavaScript library that provides a high-level interface to the WaniKani API, allowing you to fetch and manage data efficiently.

This library is designed to simplify the process of working with the WaniKani API, providing methods to fetch bundled data and manage caching effectively using IndexedDB for indexing subject data and localStorage for other data.

## Documentation

Please refer to the [documentation](https://digas99.github.io/wanikani-api-manager/docs/user/) for details on the available methods and try [this demo](https://digas99.github.io/wanikani-api-manager/docs/demo/) to get a better understanding of what each method does. You can find the source code and respective implementation of this library in [/tests](https://github.com/digas99/wanikani-api-manager/tree/main/tests).

## Quickstart Example

Example using events:

```javascript
import { WaniKaniAPIManager } from "wanikani-api-manager";

const wkManager = new WanikaniAPIManager({
   apiKey: "your_api_key_here",
});

// Function to display the kanji list for a specific level
const showKanjiList = (level, kanjiList) => {
   if (!level) return;

   console.log(`Kanji List for Level ${level}:`, kanjiList);
};

// Begin by fetching user information and the kanji list for the current level
// this is non-blocking and cached data will be returned immediately
// updated data will be fetched in the background and arrive via events
// await is needed to access cache from IndexedDB
const userInfo = await wkManager.getUserInfo();
let currentLevel = userInfo?.level;
const kanjiList = await wkManager.getKanji(currentLevel);

// this will trigger right away with cached data (might be empty if no data is cached yet)
showKanjiList(currentLevel, kanjiList);


/* Listen to the updated data from the WaniKani API */

// When the user info is updated, fetch the kanji for the expected level
wkManager.events.on('get:user', (userInfo, cached) => {
   if (userInfo) {
      currentLevel = userInfo.level; // update the current level globally
      wkManager.getKanji(currentLevel); // fetch the kanji for the updated level
   }
});

// When the kanji data is updated, display the kanji list for the current level
wkManager.events.on('get:subjects', (kanji, cached) => {
   if (kanji) showKanjiList(currentLevel, kanji);
});
```

## Development

To set up the development environment, follow these steps:

1. Clone the repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/digas99/wanikani-api-manager
   cd wanikani-api-manager
   ```
2. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```
3. Create a `.env` file in the root directory and add your WaniKani API key:
   ```plaintext
   VITE_WANIKANI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
   ```
   Replace `your_api_key_here` with your actual WaniKani API key.
4. Start the development server:
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

### Build for Production
To build the library for production, run:
```bash
npm run build
```
This will create a production-ready build in the `dist` directory. This command will also generate the documentation.

### Build Documentation
To generate the documentation, for the user or for the developer, run:
```bash
npm run build:docs-user
npm run build:docs-dev
```
